Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the initial questionnaire responses — a few follow-ups from our security team so we can close our vendor review. We want to confirm exact behavior for customer data that flows through the Hosted API:

1) If we send PII in prompt text, how long is it persisted in logs, backups, and any caching layers? Please split by: request logs, inference cache/KV, model prompt cache, and backups/snapshots.

2) What is the timeline and process for a full tenant data purge (delete all customer-derived inputs + outputs) on the Hosted plan? We need an expected SLA for erasure after an approved request.

3) Are there differences in retention between ephemeral KV/prefix caches and the durable request/usage logs? If so, please describe.

4) We also need evidence: a simple dataflow diagram and a short CSV mapping of retention windows per artifact type (request bodies, logs, traces, backups). Can you attach those?

Appreciate concise answers — our SOC team is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Evan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API — residency / retention follow-up

Kimberly / Ben — answers below for consolidation to LakeSky: please review and edit for tone.

1) Persistence by artifact (hosted API, standard plan):
- Request bodies & generated outputs: retained for 30 days by default for debugging and abuse detection. Can be configured to 0 days (disable retention) at account creation for customers that opt-in to no retention.
- Request logs / usage metadata (token counts, timestamps, route): kept for 180 days for billing and analytics; PII is redacted from billing records where present.
- Inference KV / prefix cache: ephemeral and kept in-memory on the serving host; TTL is workload-driven and typically <= 1 hour. KV entries are never written to durable backing stores in Hosted mode.
- Model prompt caches: short-lived (seconds to minutes) and purged on model swap or node recycle. No durable persistence.
- Backups / snapshots: configuration/state backups are retained for 365 days; backups do not include full request payloads by default (we snapshot configuration and model artifacts only).

2) Tenant data purge process (Hosted):
- Standard purge SLA: 7 business days to remove all stored request bodies, outputs, and caches from active and backup indexes. This includes removing entries from request stores and triggering deletion markers for any snapshots.
- Verification: After the purge, we provide a signed attest letter and internal audit log (event IDs) documenting the deletion steps. Customers with contractual needs can upgrade to a 3-business-day SLA via Dedicated plan add-on.

3) Differences between ephemeral KV/prefix caches and durable logs:
- KV/prefix caches are in-memory and transient — not part of backups. Durable logs are written to an append-only store with controlled retention. Purge requests act on both by removing durable records and invalidating/in-memory flushing cache entries via a coordinated flush command.

4) Evidence: attaching a simplified dataflow diagram and a CSV mapping retention windows. Also attaching a zip of redacted audit snippets we can share after a mutual NDA if required.

Notes / exceptions:
- We do not retrain models on raw customer prompts on Hosted by default; training pipelines are separate and only use vetted datasets.
- For regulated accounts that require geographic lock or deleted-data attestations, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments.

Marissa

Evan / Jing — thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, customer-facing summary and the requested artifacts (attached).

Executive summary (Hosted API — LakeSky AI):
- Default retention: request bodies & outputs = 30 days; billing/usage metadata = 180 days; config backups = 365 days.
- Caches: inference KV and prefix caches are in-memory (TTL typically <=1 hour) and are not written to disk on Hosted.
- Purge SLA: 7 business days from a validated request. On purge we remove request/response records from stores, invalidate caches, and mark any affected backup snapshots for deletion; we provide a deletion attestation and event IDs.
- Optional controls: customers can select no-retention at onboarding (0-day) or upgrade to Dedicated for a 3-business-day SLA and region-lock options.

Attachments included:
- redwood_dataflow_diagram.pdf — simplified flow showing where request payloads transit and which artifacts are durable vs ephemeral.
- tenant-retention-matrix.csv — per-artifact retention windows and notes.
- data-handling-evidence.zip — redacted audit snippets and sample deletion attestation (provided under existing NDA).

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/s/retention-evidence-LS-123 (artifact packages), DOCS-REDWOOD-RESIDENCY-2027-06 (internal reference).

If you want a faster SLA or geo-locked custody, Ben can share options and pricing for Dedicated/Private. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if useful.

Best,
